entries.name: start_spinner
entries.summary: Start the spinning animation on the tile

entries.name: stop_spinner
entries.summary: Stop the spinning animation on the tile.

entries.name: refresh_tile_now
entries.summary: Updates the front of the tile using the passed html. If new_html is None then render_content is called to generate the html to be displayed.

entries.name: display_status
entries.summary: Updates the front of the tile using the passed html. It looks like this might behave differently than refresh_tile_now under some circumstances. In particular, it looks like it updates pipe information if necessary.

entries.name: spin_and_refresh
entries.summary: Starts the spinner, refreshes the tile, then stops the spinner.

entries.name: widget
entries.summary: This is the method for creating widgets that can be displayed on tiles and in the notebook. See the widgets docs for details: Widgets.

entries.name: render_all_widgets
entries.summary: This renders all of the widgets that were created with the Tile Creator and which have to_render=True

entries.name: get_document_names
entries.summary: Returns a list of all document names in the current collection.

entries.name: get_current_document_name
entries.summary: Returns the name of the current document.

entries.name: get_document_data
entries.summary: For table-based documents,returns all of the data in the document represented as a dictionary. The keys of the dictionary are the values of the \__id_\_ field for each row, represented as strings.

entries.name: get_document_data_as_list
entries.summary: Returns all of the data in the document represented as a list.

entries.name: get_column_names
entries.summary: Returns a list containing the column names of the specified document. (Table documents only.)

entries.name: get_number_rows
entries.summary: Returns the number of rows in the specified document for table documents. For freeform documents, returns the number of lines.

entries.name: get_row
entries.summary: For table documents, the specified row is returned. For freeform documents, the specified line is returned. self.get_line is a synonym.

entries.name: get_cell
entries.summary: Returns the text in the specified cell.

entries.name: get_column_data
entries.summary: Get all contents of a column as a list. If document_name is not provided or is None then the content of the column from all documents is returned as one long list. (Table documents only.)

entries.name: get_column_data_dict
entries.summary: Returns a dictionary. The keys of the dictionary are the document names. Each value is a list corresponding to the values in column_name for the document. (Table documents only.)

entries.name: get_document_metadata
entries.summary: Returns a the document-level metadata for the given document. Returns a dict.

entries.name: set_cell
entries.summary: Sets the text in the specified cell. By default generates a CellChange event.

entries.name: add_document
entries.summary: Adds a new table document to the collection. Note that if the name of an existing document is given that document is overwritten.

entries.name: remove_document
entries.summary: Removes a document from the collection.

entries.name: add_freeform_document
entries.summary: Adds a new freeform document to the collection. Note that if the name of an existing document is given that document is overwritten.

entries.name: insert_row
entries.summary: Insert a new row in a document at the specified index.

entries.name: delete_row
entries.summary: Delete a row from a document.

entries.name: rename_document
entries.summary: Rename a document in the collection.

entries.name: set_document
entries.summary: This is a general utility for setting document data.

entries.name: set_column_data
entries.summary: Sets the column in a document.

entries.name: set_document_metadata
entries.summary: Sets the document_level metadata for the given document.

entries.name: set_cell_background
entries.summary: Sets the the background color of the specified cell to the given color. The color is used in an expression of the form: $(el).css("background-color", color). So color has to be something that can appear in that expression. ColorMapper.color_from_val() generates the right sort of thing.

entries.name: color_cell_text
entries.summary: Highlights the words in the target cell.

entries.name: clear_table_highlighting
entries.summary: Clears a main table highlighting.

entries.name: highlight_matching_text
entries.summary: Highlights matching text in the main table.

entries.name: display_all_rows
entries.summary: Will cause the table to display all rows. (Table documents only.)

entries.name: apply_to_rows
entries.summary: Applies the specified func to each row.

entries.name: log_it
entries.summary: Adds the given html to the log (formerly called the console).

entries.name: get_container_log
entries.summary: Returns, as a string, the current contents of the container log file. This is the log file of the container that holds the tile. All error messages go to this file. Also and print statements.

entries.name: send_tile_message
entries.summary: Sends a message to a tile with the given name. The event_name and data are passed to the named tile, which it can capture by defining a handle_tile_message method. (See Events and handlers )

entries.summary: Returns a list of the available user function names or class names. This list can be restricted to those with the specified tag. These names can then be used to access the associated function or class with get_user_function() or get_user_class().

entries.summary: When using matplotlib.pyplot to work in interactive mode, use this alternative command to generate html to display the figure. in the page. If it's false, then the html produced contains a link that references a png file hosted on the server.

entries.summary: Given a bokeh plot, this returns html to display the plot. The entirety of what this method is below, in case you want to do something slightly different. However, doing something other than Resources("inline") can cause problems, especially when loading a saved project.

entries.summary: This command imports a module into the global namespace. So, for example, global_import("nltk") within render_content would make nltk available within all method calls in your tile.

entries.name: handle_button_click
entries.summary: A call to this handler is generated when the the user clicks a button within the body of a tile. value is the button value. The default handler has no effect.

entries.name: handle_select_change
entries.canonical: def handle_select_change(self, value, doc_name, active_row_index, select_name)
entries.summary: This handler is called when the user changes the value of a select element in the body of the tile. value is the value selected. select_name is the value of the name property assigned in the html for your select component. The default handler does nothing.

entries.name: handle_tile_row_click
entries.summary: This handler is called when the user clicks on a row in a table that is displayed on the tile. Note that the row must have the class row-clickable. This can be accomplished by calling html_table with click_type=row-clickable. clicked_row contains a list of the values in the cells in the row. The default handler does nothing.

entries.name: handle_tile_word_click
entries.summary: This handler is called when the user clicks on a word on the front of the tile. Note that the word must be within an element with the class word-clickable. The default handler selects all appearances of the clicked word in the main data table.

entries.name: handle_form_submit
entries.summary: Called when the user clicks submit in a form within the body of a tile. form_data is a dictionary in which the keys are the names of elements in the form, and the values are their current values. Note that one of these entries will correspond to the submit button itself. The default handler does nothing.

entries.name: handle_textarea_change
entries.summary: Called when the user the user changes the contents of a textarea DOM element on the front of the tile. value is the new content of the textarea. The default handler does nothing.

entries.name: handle_size_change
entries.summary: The size of the current tile has been changed by the user. The default handler does nothing.

entries.name: handle_doc_change
entries.summary: The visible document in the main data has been changed. The default handler does nothing.

entries.name: handle_text_select
entries.summary: The has selected text within the main table. The default handler does nothing.

entries.name: handle_cell_change
entries.signature: handle_cell_change(self, column_header, row_index, old_content, new_content, doc_name)
entries.canonical: def handle_cell_change(self, column_header, row_index, old_content, new_content, doc_name)
entries.summary: A cell in the main data table has been changed. The default handler does nothing.

entries.name: handle_freeform_text_change
entries.summary: The text of a freeform data table has been changed. The default handler does nothing.

entries.name: handle_pipe_update
entries.summary: The value of a pipe has changed. The default handler does nothing.

entries.name: modify_options
entries.summary: Sometimes you might want the options in a tile to vary based on some conditions. For example, you might want some options to appear or disappear based on the value of another boolean option. This can be accomplished by adding a modify_options method to your tile.

entries.name: handle_option_change
entries.summary: Called when the user changes an individual option on the back of a tile. opt_name is the name of the option and value is the new value.

entries.name: handle_tile_message
entries.summary: This handler is called when the a message is sent using the send_tile_message command. Note that this handler can return a value.
